1. Executive Summary & Variant Perception

S&P Global Inc. (NYSE: SPGI) represents one of the quintessential "capital-light tollbooths" on global capitalism. The company provides critical credit ratings, benchmark equity indices, enterprise financial intelligence, and commodity price reporting—financial infrastructure without which global capital markets cannot efficiently function. Following the tax-free spin-off of its Mobility division (Mobility Global, NYSE: MBGL) on July 1, 2026, SPGI has transformed into a pure-play, high-margin, asset-light financial compounder.

At $408.69 per share, SPGI trades at approximately 21.0x management’s FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance. The core investment thesis centers on the structural durability of its market positions, massive incremental operating margins, and an accelerated share cannibal strategy enabled by the divestment of lower-margin assets.

Variant Perception vs. Consensus Wall Street View

The market consensus views SPGI through the lens of interest rate sensitivity and cyclical debt issuance, fearing that structural growth in private credit will disintermediate public bond markets and permanently lower Ratings transaction volumes. Our fundamental analysis reveals three key variant perspectives:

  • Private Credit is a Net Monetization Driver, Not a Threat: Rather than eroding Ratings revenue, private market credit expansion is generating a new revenue tailwind. SPGI's private markets rating revenue surged 60% YoY in Q2 2026. Concurrently, Market Intelligence is selling specialized valuation feeds, credit risk models, and direct data feeds to alternative asset managers requiring institutional transparency.
  • Unappreciated Tollbooth Economics of Passive Indexing: S&P Dow Jones Indices delivered its 13th consecutive record revenue quarter in Q2 2026, with exchange-traded fund (ETF) assets under management tied to S&P indices reaching $6.35 Trillion. The institutional shift toward passive indexing creates a permanent, royalty-like revenue stream with 71.5% operating margins that require virtually zero reinvestment capital.
  • Aggressive Post-Spin Cannibal Share Buybacks: Following the separation of Mobility, management under CEO Martina Cheung has committed to returning 100%+ of adjusted Free Cash Flow to shareholders. The company is repurchasing over $7.0 Billion of stock in FY2026 alone—shrinking the total diluted share count by over 5% annually and compounding Owner Earnings per share through macro cycles.
CEO Commentary — Q2 2026 Earnings Call:

"We delivered another strong quarter, with record results in two of our benchmark businesses—Ratings and Indices—and we successfully launched Mobility Global as an independent public company... All of this, along with the talent of our employees, positions us well for increasingly profitable long-term growth." — Martina Cheung, President & CEO

Unit Economics & The Four Moat Pillars

SPGI’s economic engine is defined by exceptional pricing power and operating leverage. Once a credit rating methodology or equity index is established, the marginal cost of rating an additional tranche of debt or licensing an index to a new fund manager is nearly zero. Incremental operating margins in the Ratings and Indices divisions regularly exceed 80%. The business model is fortified by four moat pillars:

  1. Government-Sanctioned Oligopoly (Ratings): S&P Global Ratings operates within a regulatory-sanctioned duopoly alongside Moody's. Global fixed-income markets operate under strict credit rating requirements defined by central banks, pension funds, and sovereign regulations. Institutional investors are legally mandated to hold bonds rated by a Nationally Recognized Statistical Rating Organization (NRSRO). Issuers pay SPGI because an unrated bond demands a substantial yield penalty.
  2. The S&P 500 Network Effect (Indices): S&P Dow Jones Indices owns the recognized benchmarks for equity market performance. Fund managers are measured against the S&P 500, forcing institutional mandates to hold S&P-indexed assets. With $6.35 Trillion in ETF AUM tied to S&P indices, capital inflows automatically drive asset-linked licensing revenues directly to SPGI's bottom line.
  3. Embedded Enterprise Workflow Lock-in (Market Intelligence): Capital IQ and RatingsXpress data feeds are deeply integrated into investment bank valuation models, private equity workflows, and corporate treasury management systems. Replacing SPGI data requires retraining analysts and re-engineering risk architecture, creating customer retention rates exceeding 93%.
  4. Pricing Tollbooth in Physical Commodities (Commodity Insights / Platts): Platts assessments serve as the underlying settlement price for physical crude oil, natural gas, and metal contracts globally. When energy counterparties trade physical cargoes, contracts specify "Platts Dated Brent plus/minus a spread." This makes Platts benchmark access non-negotiable for global energy participants.
Strategic Takeaway:

SPGI requires under 2% of annual revenues in physical Capital Expenditures to maintain its infrastructure ($195M CapEx vs. $15.34B Revenue in FY2025). The resulting Owner Cash Flow is almost entirely available to management for opportunistic stock repurchases and strategicbolt-on acquisitions.

Owner Earnings & SBC Dilution Audit

Management frequently reports headline Free Cash Flow without deducting stock-based grants. In FY 2025, SPGI generated $5.57 billion in GAAP Operating Cash Flow and incurred $236 million in SBC alongside $195 million in total capital expenditures. For the first half of 2026, GAAP Operating Cash Flow reached $2.48 billion, with Q2 contributing $1.44 billion. Subtracting Q2 capital expenditures ($52M) and Q2 SBC expense ($95M) yields a true Q2 2026 Owner Cash Flow of $1.29 billion.

Share Repurchase Cannibal vs. Dilution Dynamics

While SBC causes an annual share dilution rate of roughly 0.15% to 0.20% (~0.3M to 0.5M shares granted per year), SPGI's aggressive share buyback cannibal program completely overwhelms this drag. Management repurchased $1.0 billion of common stock in Q1 2026 and another $1.0 billion in Q2 2026, executing $2.0 billion in buybacks over the first six months alone. Following the successful tax-free spin-off of its Mobility division (Mobility Global, MBGL) on July 1, 2026, management reiterated its commitment to return 100% or more of adjusted Free Cash Flow through dividends and buybacks (~$4.5 billion targeted for full-year 2026). Net diluted shares outstanding have fallen systematically from over 330 million post-IHS Markit merger to ~295 million.

Balance Sheet Reality & Capital Structure Bridge

As of Q2 2026 official balance sheet filings, SPGI maintains a fortress capital structure designed to withstand macro debt market volatility:

  • Cash, Cash Equivalents & Restricted Cash: $4.141 Billion.
  • Short-Term Debt & Commercial Paper: $825 Million.
  • Long-Term Senior Unsecured Notes: $14.345 Billion.
  • Total Debt & Obligations: $15.170 Billion.
  • Net Debt Position: $11.029 Billion ($15.170B Total Debt minus $4.141B Total Cash).
Capital Allocation Strategy & Moat Protection: SPGI operates at a comfortable net leverage ratio of ~1.8x to 2.0x EBITDA. Because the business requires minimal physical capital reinvestment (CapEx consumes less than 4% of operating cash flow), nearly every dollar of Owner Earnings is available for opportunistic M&A (such as acquiring datacenterHawk and Agusto & Co. in July 2026) or returning directly to shareholders via dividends and share count reduction.

Leadership Succession & Governance Architecture

In November 2024, Martina L. Cheung assumed the role of President and CEO, succeeding long-time CEO Douglas L. Peterson. Cheung previously led S&P Global Ratings and Market Intelligence, driving high operating margins and spearheading major structural integration projects including the IHS Markit transaction.

Governance & Alignment Highlights:
  • Independent Chair Structure: Ian Livingston serves as Independent Non-Executive Chairman of the Board, enforcing strict oversight and separation between executive management and board governance.
  • Performance-Linked Executive Compensation: CEO Martina Cheung's compensation package (~$12.8M total) is heavily weighted toward long-term equity incentive awards (LTIP) conditioned on multi-year relative Total Shareholder Return (TSR), organic revenue growth, and Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) targets.
  • Rigorous Ownership Guidelines & Clawbacks: Executives are subject to stock ownership requirements (6x base salary for CEO) and strict clawback provisions covering misstatements, compliance failures, or material detrimental conduct.

Section 5: Warren Buffett Owner Earnings & Intrinsic Value

To determine the true intrinsic value of S&P Global Inc. (NYSE: SPGI) at the current share price of $408.69, we look past accounting net income and Wall Street short-term earnings metrics, anchoring our evaluation in the intrinsic value methodology outlined by Warren Buffett in his Berkshire Hathaway Shareholder Letters (notably the 1986, 1995, 1999, and 2018 essays). We explicitly reject arbitrary exit multiples, which Charlie Munger rightly dismissed as "relying on a greater fool in Year 5," and instead discount the projected cash flow stream back to present value using localized sovereign rates.

1. Baseline Owner Earnings Calculation (1986 Shareholder Letter Framework)

Buffett defines Owner Earnings as Operating Cash Flow minus Maintenance Capital Expenditures minus Stock-Based Compensation (SBC). SBC is treated as a 100% real cash cost—if executive talent and quantitative analysts were not compensated with equity, S&P Global would be forced to pay equivalent cash salaries to prevent talent drain.

2. Capital-Light Moat & Working Capital Float Discipline

S&P Global is an elite, capital-light cash generator. Capital expenditures represent roughly 1.3% of annual revenue, requiring negligible physical reinvestment to maintain its competitive position. Furthermore, the company operates with negative working capital in its Market Intelligence and Indices segments, collecting upfront annual subscription and licensing fees before delivering services. In accordance with Buffett’s principles regarding insurance float (1995 & 2002 Berkshire Letters), this unearned revenue liability ($3,929 million as of Q2 2026) acts as an interest-free customer float that funds organic technology upgrades and bolt-on acquisitions.

4. Localized Sovereign Discount Rate

Because S&P Global’s cash flows are denominated in USD and earned across international capital markets, we ground the valuation in the US 10-Year Treasury Yield (~4.20%) rather than arbitrary hurdle rates. Adding an Equity Risk Premium (ERP) of 4.30% to account for capital market debt issuance volatility yields a Base Case discount rate of 8.50% (Bear Case: 9.00%; Bull Case: 8.00%).

5. Share Buyback Cannibal Compounding

Following management's commitment to repurchase over $7.0 billion in common stock in 2026 following the Mobility spin-off, S&P Global exemplifies Buffett’s "Share Buyback Cannibal" framework (1999 & 2018 Letters). By retiring 2.0% to 3.5% of its shares annually at sensible prices, the company directly compounds per-share Owner Earnings over a 10-year holding period.

Section 6: What Breaks The Thesis & Invalidation Pre-Mortem

To maintain objective surveillance on S&P Global, we establish explicit execution risk factors, structural vulnerability points, and quantifiable pre-mortem falsification triggers that would invalidate the long-term investment thesis.

1. Primary Operational & Macro Vulnerabilities

  • Credit Issuance Freeze & Refinancing Cliff Delay: S&P Ratings generates a substantial portion of profits from transaction fees on debt issuance. Prolonged high benchmark interest rates or credit spread spikes that freeze corporate bond issuance directly impair high-margin Ratings transaction revenue.
  • Disintermediation & Private Credit Expansion: The rapid growth of non-bank private credit markets, where bilateral loans bypass traditional public credit rating requirements, threatens to reduce the total addressable market (TAM) for billed issuance in public bond markets.
  • AI Disruption of Desktop Financial Terminals: Market Intelligence relies on recurring desktop subscription seats. Generative AI agents capable of web-scraping, aggregating financial data, and writing financial models could erode pricing power for traditional desktop subscriptions if proprietary analytics are not defended.
  • Regulatory Interventions & Conflict Oversight: Increased regulatory scrutiny by the SEC, ESMA, or global market authorities regarding rating agency fee structures or competition rules could restrict pricing adjustments or increase legal compliance costs.

Thesis Pre-Mortem & Falsification Triggers:

  • Ratings Revenue Compression: Two consecutive quarters of YoY decline exceeding 12% in S&P Ratings transaction revenue due to private credit substitution or debt issuance collapse.
  • ROIC Erosion: Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) falling below 18% (excluding goodwill adjustments), signaling capital-inefficient bolt-on M&A or failing integration of new assets.
  • SBC Dilution Spike: Stock-based compensation rising above 6.0% of operating cash flow, eroding the per-share cash returns of common equity holders.
  • Margin Contraction: Adjusted operating margin in Market Intelligence declining by more than 150 basis points year-over-year due to competitive pricing pressure from financial AI agents.
